Security review (ADR-006 section 6) found one MEDIUM and one latent bug, both fixed in this session: the settings UI advertised the strict ruleset as gating reads, which neither the ADR nor the code does; and a PATCH could store auto_approve=true on a readonly workspace because the resolved value was only written back when it differed from the row. It verified clean: cross-user workspace access on every REST and WS path, auto-approval unable to reach a Google or MCP tool, no LocalBackend reachable from app/, the deny guard firing on .env and .pem and .ssh after approval, the new strip_url_credentials keyword compatible with all seven existing callers, and SANDBOX_SERVICE_TOKEN never leaving SecretStr

limitations: Shrink pass ran (2 parallel reviewers) and changed the code: replaced a 25-line hand-rolled ruleset with the library PERMISSIVE_RULESET it duplicated exactly; deleted build_test_backend, whose LocalBackend import contradicted the module boundary rule; deleted the dead CODING_TOOL_NAMES; reduced aclose() to backend.stop() after confirming neither sandbox class has close(); replaced the ORM row with a frozen WorkspacePolicy value so the agent layer holds no detached row; partitioned the approval list once instead of walking it three times; dropped the consumer-less workspace_attached event; and moved the picker onto the repo Select primitive (it was the only raw select element in frontend/src)

strict and default build an identical toolset - the only effect of strict is that auto-approve can never be enabled. That matches ADR-006 section 4, which does not gate reads; the settings copy was corrected to say so rather than implementing read gating, which would need an approval bridge the library ask_callback cannot provide
The auto_approved=true tool-span attribute ADR-006 section 4 asks for is not implemented; auto-approved calls are recorded in the application log and a WS event instead

No end-to-end run against a real sandboxd: the approval, denial, and readonly paths are proved with an in-memory StateBackend driving the real toolkit through a real Agent, not over HTTP to the service
No browser check of the workspace picker beyond type-check, lint, and vitest
reason: ADR-006 decided that a chat turn may name a coding workspace and act on it through sandboxed file and shell tools, but the AssistantAgent still registers no file, shell, or git tool, so a workspace row is inert: the product cannot perform the coding tasks it was envisioned for. This adds pydantic-ai-backend's console toolset behind a per-turn CodingToolkit built the way ResearchToolkit is, executing only through a sandbox backend, with write and execute gated by the existing deferred-approval loop unless the workspace auto-approves.
risks: auto_approve grants unattended write and execute inside the sandbox for the selected workspace; the deny guard still blocks secrets and destructive commands, but ordinary workspace files can be changed without a prompt

RemoteSandbox is a sync client offloaded to the shared asyncio default thread pool, which also serves the per-turn MCP SSRF revalidation; concurrent long execute calls can delay that check. Sizing a dedicated pool is deferred to ADR-006 open question 3 (quotas)
No sandboxd service exists in any Compose stack yet, so ENABLE_CODING cannot be turned on in a Compose deployment until the next session lands it
rollback: git revert restores the code and removes the dependency from pyproject/uv.lock; run uv sync --directory backend afterwards. No migration and no schema change in this session. If ENABLE_CODING was turned on in a deployment, unset it (and the SANDBOX_ vars) - otherwise the reverted build has no coding toolkit but the flag remains set, and the new Settings validator will refuse to start if the sandbox vars are half-configured. Any sandbox sessions already created live in the sandbox service and are reaped there, not by this repository.
security_impact: This is the privilege expansion ADR-006 records approval for: with ENABLE_CODING=true and a workspace selected, the assistant gains write_file, edit_file, execute, ls, read_file, glob, and grep inside a sandbox. ADR-006 section 6 also requires a security review before this record; it ran, and its outcome is recorded under effects. Mitigations, each tested: the three mutating tools are deferred approvals resolved by the existing browser dialog; auto-approval is scoped to those three names and only for a default-ruleset workspace that opted in, so a Google or MCP mutation in the same batch still asks (every other tool source is name-prefixed, verified); a readonly workspace registers no mutating tool at all; the backend is wrapped with the library PERMISSIVE_RULESET via guarding(), so secret files (.env, *.pem, .ssh) stay unreadable and destructive commands stay blocked even after the user approves; background-shell tools are not registered because they bypass that guard and are unimplemented on both permitted sandboxes; nothing under app/ imports LocalBackend, so the ADR-006 execution-boundary rule is greppable; and Settings now refuses ENABLE_CODING at startup without a sandbox URL and token. Coding is off by default, so a deployment that does not opt in is unchanged.
summary: Attach a sandboxed coding toolkit to a chat turn that names a workspace
